title: UAE Launches Five-Year Multiple-Entry Tourist Visa Open to All Nationalities
excerpt: The new visa allows stays of up to 90 days per visit with no sponsor needed, costs around ₹97,300 including a refundable deposit, and lets holders convert to work or Golden Visa status without leaving the country.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • UAE launched a five-year multiple-entry tourist visa for all nationalities on July 16.
  • Visa allows stays of up to 90 days per visit, totaling 180 days per year.
  • Total cost is approximately AED 3,713, including a refundable AED 3,000 deposit.
  • Applications are processed online within 2-5 working days via gdrfad.gov.ae.
  • Visa holders can convert to work or Golden Visa without leaving the UAE.

Key Takeaways

  • UAE's GDRFA Dubai announced a 5-year multiple-entry tourist visa on July 16, open to all nationalities
  • Holders can stay up to 90 days per visit and up to 180 days per year, with no sponsor required
  • Total cost is approximately AED 3,713 (around ₹97,300), including a refundable AED 3,000 security deposit
  • Applications are processed online within 2-5 working days via gdrfad.gov.ae
  • The visa does not grant work rights, but holders can convert to a work or Golden Visa without leaving the UAE

For the millions of Indians who treat Dubai as a second home — for business, shopping, family visits, or simply a long weekend away — the visa arithmetic has just changed dramatically. The General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs in Dubai announced on July 16 a new five-year multiple-entry tourist visa that eliminates the need for repeated applications, sponsorship requirements, and the anxiety of single-entry paperwork.

The visa is open to all nationalities, requires no UAE-based sponsor, and allows stays of up to 90 days per entry — extendable to a cumulative 180 days per year. For a diaspora community that already drives the largest share of tourist traffic to the UAE, this is a quiet but consequential shift in how they can engage with the country.

What It Costs and What You Need

The total fee comes to approximately AED 3,713, which works out to around ₹97,300 at current exchange rates. This includes a refundable security deposit of AED 3,000 — a mechanism designed to ensure compliance with visa conditions, returned when the visa expires or is cancelled.

The application process is entirely online through gdrfad.gov.ae, with processing times of two to five working days. Required documents include a passport valid for at least six months, proof of health insurance covering the UAE stay, a bank statement showing a minimum balance of $4,000, and a confirmed return ticket.

> **"Indians sent more than $48 billion in remittances from the Gulf region in 2025, and the UAE hosts the largest Indian expatriate population in the world — more than 3.5 million people."**
"This visa really changes the equation for frequent travellers — especially business professionals and families with ties to the UAE who were previously navigating 30-day or 90-day single-entry visas every few months," says Farah Al-Suwaidi, an immigration consultant at Fragomen Dubai.

Who Benefits Most

India is the UAE's largest source market for tourism, and the five-year visa addresses a persistent friction point. Until now, Indian travellers without a UAE residence visa had to apply for a new tourist visa for each trip — a process involving paperwork, processing fees, and wait times that added up fast for frequent visitors.

The new visa is particularly significant for several groups. Business professionals who travel to Dubai or Abu Dhabi multiple times a year for meetings, trade shows, or client visits can now enter freely without reapplying. Families with relatives working in the UAE — a community numbering in the hundreds of thousands — gain the flexibility to visit without coordination around visa windows.

Property owners, too, stand to benefit. Indians are among the top foreign buyers of Dubai real estate, and the multiple-entry visa simplifies the logistics of checking on properties, meeting tenants, or simply spending extended periods in the city without a residence visa.

What It Does Not Cover

The visa explicitly does not grant work rights. Holders cannot take up employment, freelance, or conduct commercial activities under its terms. However, in a notable provision, the UAE allows holders to convert the tourist visa to a work visa or a Golden Visa without leaving the country — removing the traditional requirement of exiting and re-entering on a different visa category.

Application Process Simplified
›Online application at gdrfad.gov.ae
›Processing time: 2-5 working days
›Documents needed: passport, health insurance, bank statement, return ticket
›Visa linked electronically to passport

This conversion pathway is significant for professionals exploring UAE job opportunities. Rather than travelling on a tourist visa, returning home, and then waiting for a work visa to be processed, they can transition directly from within the country once an employment offer is secured.

The Broader Context

The five-year tourist visa is part of a wider push by the UAE to simplify its immigration framework and attract longer-term visitors. The country has progressively liberalised visa rules over the past three years, introducing remote work visas, expanding the Golden Visa programme, and relaxing residency requirements for retirees and investors.

For the Indian diaspora specifically, the move reflects a recognition of the community's economic weight. Indians sent more than $48 billion in remittances from the Gulf region in 2025, and the UAE hosts the largest Indian expatriate population in the world — more than 3.5 million people.

The new visa does not replace existing options. The standard 30-day and 90-day tourist visas remain available for shorter stays, and the 10-year Golden Visa continues to serve investors, entrepreneurs, and exceptional talent. But for the broad middle of frequent visitors who fall outside those categories, the five-year visa fills a gap that has long been obvious.

How to Apply

Who Benefits from the New Visa?
›Frequent business travelers can enter without reapplying.
›Families can visit relatives without visa coordination.
›Property owners can manage real estate more easily.
›Indians are the largest tourist group in the UAE.

Applications are accepted online at gdrfad.gov.ae. Applicants must upload a passport copy, health insurance documentation, a bank statement meeting the $4,000 minimum, and a return flight booking. Once approved, the visa is delivered electronically and linked to the passport — no physical stamp required.

The refundable AED 3,000 deposit is charged at the time of application and returned upon visa expiry or cancellation, provided no violations have occurred during the validity period. The remaining fees cover processing and administrative costs.
